title: LSDE 2.8: exporters now run from the Export button, LSDE links open text keys, and AI tasks skip translations by default
author: djmisterjon
selftext:
I make LSDE, a desktop editor for game dialogue, localization and narrative scenes.   
**Version 2.8 is mostly about the path between the editor and the game engine.**

**What changed**

* An exporter can now run with the Export button in the header: tick "With the Export button" under "When it goes out". The button writes the language files first, then runs the ticked exporters one after the other, and stays available even when there are no language files to write.
* An LSDE link (lsde://) now opens text keys as well as scenes, and creates the key empty if it doesn't exist yet. A button in Unity, Godot or a ticket can lead straight to a line.
* Correct, Rewrite, Lengthen, Shorten, Continue, Fill in and Compose now skip translations by default and work on the main language. A selection made inside a translation is still processed, and "Skip every translation" can be unticked at any time.
* The default fallback LLM gets a temp-mail.id button next to the other disposable accounts, to create a free account.

**Why**

Until now, each exporter ran from its own button or on save, so a project that hands its data to an engine repeated the same steps after every fix. And a correction pass over a whole folder should not rewrite translations nobody asked it to touch.

How do you connect your engine's editor to your dialogue text? Keys in code, a lookup tool, or links like these?
